x-notes: DRAFT, NOT BUILDABLE YET: every remaining PLACEHOLDER_* value below must be replaced by a real pin before a build.
numpy comes from io.qt.PySide.BaseApp (6.11), so it is not installed from a wheel here.

The scanner driver is an EXTERNAL dependency: the owner's fork (github.com/bearyjd/opticfilm135i-linux) pinned at commit eaa6f88, which has the calibration stop gate default 'enforce'. Upstream cgillinger master (6270867) has the gate OFF by default and exits 4 on slide scans here, so it is NOT used. Nothing from Plustek or the vendor driver is vendored here.

--device=all is the broad choice for raw USB access (07b3:1436): it works on the host but is untested inside the sandbox, and it also grants GPU access that Qt Quick may rely on, so narrowing to --device=usb needs --device=dri alongside and is untested.

modules.name: python-dependencies
build-commands: pip3 install --verbose --exists-action=i --no-index --find-links="file://${PWD}" --prefix=${FLATPAK_DEST} --no-deps pillow tifffile opencv-python-headless pyusb

modules.name: opticfilm-linux
build-commands: printf '#!/bin/sh\nPYTHONPATH=/app/lib/opticfilm exec python3 -c "from opticfilm_linux.app.qt.app import main; raise SystemExit(main())" "$@"\n' > /app/bin/opticfilm
printf '#!/bin/sh\nPYTHONPATH=/app/lib/opticfilm exec python3 -c "from opticfilm_linux.cli import main; raise SystemExit(main())" "$@"\n' > /app/bin/ofscan
